data.answer: Hello! How can I help you today?
I am your personal chatbot assistant — here to answer your questions and help you learn!
I'm just a program, but I'm doing great! Thanks for asking 😊
Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its simplicity and readability.
AI stands for Artificial Intelligence. It refers to systems that perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence.
Machine Learning is a subset of AI that allows computers to learn from data and improve automatically.
SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to manage and manipulate data in relational databases.
Flask is a lightweight Python web framework used to build web applications quickly and easily.
A chatbot is an AI program that simulates human conversation and provides automated responses.
A chatbot works by matching user input to predefined keywords or using AI models to understand and generate natural responses.
AI is the broader concept of machines simulating human intelligence. Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI that focuses on learning from data.
NLP (Natural Language Processing) is a branch of AI that helps computers understand, interpret, and respond to human language.
Deep Learning is a type of Machine Learning that uses neural networks with many layers to process complex data like images or speech.

Strategy_Purpose.description: Defines the 'Why' — the core reason and expected outcomes for building the chatbot.
questions: What is the single biggest problem this chatbot is trying to solve?
Who exactly will be using this chatbot (target audience)?
Why would someone use this chatbot over other options like calling or emailing?
How will we measure the chatbot’s success (KPIs or metrics)?

Functionality_Scope.description: Defines the 'What' — what the chatbot can do and what systems it connects with.
questions: What are the top 3–5 tasks users should be able to complete?
What types of questions will the chatbot answer (simple, transactional, complex)?
Which systems should the chatbot integrate with (e.g., CRM, calendar, database)?
What happens when the chatbot doesn’t know an answer — is there a human handover process?

Design_Personality.description: Defines the 'How' — the chatbot’s persona, tone, and user interaction style.
questions: What is the chatbot’s name and personality (formal, friendly, casual)?
What tone of voice and language style should it use?
How will conversations start (welcome messages, menus, or free-form text)?
What will the chatbot say when it doesn’t understand something?

Technical_Maintenance.description: Defines the 'Where' — technical implementation and long-term upkeep.
questions: Where will the chatbot be available (website, WhatsApp, Messenger, Slack)?
What type of bot will it be — rule-based or AI/NLP-powered?
What kind of user data will it collect, and how will that data be stored securely?
Who will maintain and update the chatbot after launch?
